actions: Verify the live request/resource locks and current owner token immediately before the write/effect; retain the supplied current ownership and absence of unresolved effects.
Verify the recorded exact acceptance and pending prerequisites, persist an action intent with target/action/attempt identity, then perform the accepted injected action once.
Record the attributable result; report completion only if evidenced, or failure/unknown and corresponding holds if that is observed.
records: Keep original inputs, authority, instruction/configuration binding and acceptance.
Append intent before submission, then actual observations/evidence and next action under the current owner token; keep execution and reporting events separate.
outcome: Authorized action proceeds under exclusive ownership; its actual observed result determines the execution outcome.

actions: Report resource-unresolved and hold the shared browser effect.
Resolve the canonical actual profile/session from authoritative configuration; do not invent a per-Page resource key.
records: Under verified request ownership, retain the unresolved profile identity, affected action, blocker report obligation and next action to resolve identity and obtain resource ownership.
outcome: Blocked on canonical shared-resource identification; no shared effect.

actions: Use the same canonical profile lock domain for both requests; each retains its own request lock and journal.
Only the executor that obtains demonstrable live exclusive profile ownership may submit its accepted action after persisting intent.
The other records a wait/blocker only in its own request, promptly reports it and releases safely without waiting while holding another contested resource.
Handover only after the former operation completes or is verifiably stopped; lock availability alone does not settle remote operations.
records: Preserve separate original inputs, acceptances, owner tokens, action attempts and resource-contention observations for A and B.
Record the winning acquisition and losing wait without asserting which wins; preserve any resulting uncertain effect across handover.
outcome: Shared effects are serialized by actual profile ownership; no concurrent shared-profile action or merged request history.

actions: Report ownership-unavailable and hold the action.
Do not replace unreadable ownership evidence, assume expiry, or acquire substitute ownership based on that assumption.
records: In the executor own request where its ownership is verifiable, retain the unreadable resource evidence and operation, blocked effect, report obligation and next action to restore trustworthy ownership evidence.
If request storage/ownership also cannot be verified, use the available authorized requester route without inventing durable writes.
outcome: Blocked; no shared effect until ownership is verifiable.

actions: Retain action A as unknown; hold another attempt and all dependent effects.
Recover the original attempt and reconcile attributable native evidence matching target, content, attempt and available identifiers.

If acceptance is confirmed, retain the effect and do not repeat. If positive no-effect evidence is obtained, renew authority/prerequisite checks and current ownership, record the next action and persist a new intent before a new attempt.
If evidence remains inconclusive, retain the hold and report the uncertainty; disconnect or an empty search is not proof of no effect.
records: Preserve original intent, attempt identity, disconnect observations and unknown outcome; append reconciliation evidence and next action without rewriting history.
outcome: No blind retry; further action depends on authoritative reconciliation.

actions: Reject A use of its old owner token; A performs no write or effect after safe handover to B.
If A later seeks ownership, require fresh exclusive acquisition after B safely releases, then read the current history and obtain a current owner token before any protected operation.
records: Preserve the safe handover and B current ownership; A may report its ownership conflict through the available requester route without writing the protected request.
Retain any unresolved outcomes and pending actions across subsequent acquisition.
outcome: Stale owner A is fenced by the cooperative ownership checks; B remains the valid current owner.

actions: Both contend for the same stable OS-backed request lock before initialization or writes; never unlink/recreate the lock.
Only the live exclusive winner sets a current owner token, reads existing history for resume and proceeds with applicable pending work.
The loser reports ownership conflict through the requester route and does not write R1, create duplicate acceptance or allocate a replacement resume request.
records: Winner preserves R1 original identity, inputs, binding, acceptance and prior effects, appending events only under current ownership.
Loser invents no request journal update; retain the conflict through its authorized reporting route.
outcome: Exactly one current writer/executor for R1; ownership winner is not assumed in advance.

actions: Invoke the configured report injection with R1 identity, actual outcome/reason, confirmed effects, outstanding work and any required intervention.
Preserve the supplied submission acknowledgement and do not resend the same incident.
Do not equate task acceptance with successful execution, or report submission with delivery or reading.
records: Keep task acceptance evidence and actual execution observations separately from report content, obligation/incident identity, attempt and native submission acknowledgement.
Mark communication submitted; execution status reflects its own evidence.
outcome: Report submission confirmed; delivery/reading are unproved and execution is reported truthfully from its evidence.

actions: Hold work that requires the configured account login and promptly invoke the report injection for customer intervention.
Identify the required interactive login and the blocked pending action; do not invent account access or bypass login.
After intervention, revalidate unfinished prerequisites and current ownership before any accepted pending action.
records: Retain R1 original inputs, confirmed earlier effects, login blocker, report content/obligation/attempt and actual submission outcome.
Next action is customer interactive login followed by prerequisite revalidation; communication remains independently pending/unknown/submitted as observed.
outcome: Execution blocked on customer intervention and blocker promptly reported or retained as an outstanding report obligation.

actions: Record the configured customer-portal communication outage and retain its pending report obligation; expose the gap through any available authorized requester route.
Continue the accepted, authorized, executable document export under current ownership and persisted pre-action intent; do not add a reporting-availability acceptance gate.
Record export observations and invoke the configured reporting procedure for its outcome; preserve outstanding communication until the portal can be used.
Do not substitute a channel, recipient or identity without authority or diagnose missing credentials from temporary unavailability.
records: Keep acceptance, export intent/attempt and actual execution result distinct from failed communication attempt and pending obligation/content.
Record restored-portal reporting as the next communication action; do not infer export success merely because work was executable.
outcome: Independent export work continues; communication outage remains visible and pending without a fully-reported success claim.

actions: Fail validation with missing-report-configuration; do not guess a recipient, identity or alternate report injection.
Apply the decision injection to record the configuration blocker, hold Execute and explain it through an available authorized requester route.
records: Preserve the absent required recipient configuration distinctly from an explicit empty value and from a temporary channel outage.
Retain validation findings, truthful decision, reporting gap and next action to obtain required configuration; no acceptance or task submission is invented.
outcome: Validation blocked by missing required recipient configuration; no execution.

actions: Retain the confirmed report submission for incident I1 and do not resend it merely because execution remains failed.
Report a genuinely new incident only if the injected procedure calls for it; do not invent follow-up work or automatic task retry.
records: Preserve I1 content, obligation/attempt identity and submission acknowledgement, alongside the separate failed execution evidence and existing next action.
Do not mark submission as delivered/read or change the failed execution status.
outcome: I1 remains submitted and execution remains failed; no duplicate report or business retry.

actions: Retain report attempt N1 as unknown and hold another send.
Reconcile authoritative native submission evidence for the same incident, content, attempt and available identifiers.
If accepted, retain acknowledgement without resend. Permit a new send only on positive no-effect evidence with renewed checks, ownership and recorded next action.
If uncertainty persists, retain the obligation and expose the gap through an available authorized requester route without substituting a destination.
records: Keep the original incident/obligation, N1 attempt, content and timeout evidence unchanged; append reconciliation observations and next action.
Communication is unknown until resolved; execution evidence and confirmed business effects remain independent.
outcome: Unknown send is reconciled before any repeat; no blind resend or delivery claim.

actions: Resume the explicit existing R1 under fresh current request ownership after its safe recorded release; recover original inputs, authority, complete bound instruction/configuration identities, journal and pending communication.
Verify the retained binding and recover only pending communication; do not rebind to newer instructions or repeat the confirmed execution.
Reconcile any previously unknown report attempt before sending; for the retained unsent pending obligation, persist report intent and submit through the restored configured route.
Record the native reporting outcome; do not infer delivery or reading from acknowledgement.
records: Preserve confirmed execution, safe ownership release/history, original binding and prior reporting observations.
Append new ownership, report obligation/content/attempt, intent and native submission evidence or truthful pending/unknown status; next action follows that outcome.
outcome: Reporting-only recovery of R1; confirmed business execution is never replayed and communication closes only to the extent evidenced.
